item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 151107
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Tue Sep 15 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Depression Norbert, located well east of the Hawaiian Islands, and
on Tropical Depression Fifteen-E, located well west-southwest of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Southwest of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form well offshore of southwestern
Mexico by the end of the week or over the weekend. Environmental
conditions appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter
while the system moves west-northwestward to northwestward at about
10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Depression Fifteen-E Public Advisory Number 8
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Tue Sep 15 2026 
000
WTPZ35 KNHC 151445
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Fifteen-E Advisory Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP152026
Issued by the NWS Weather Prediction Center College Park MD
800 AM PDT Tue Sep 15 2026
 
...DEPRESSION CONTINUES MOVING WESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.1N 123.9W
ABOUT 1025 MI...1650 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 260 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression
Fifteen-E was located near latitude 16.1 North, longitude 123.9
West. The depression is moving toward the west near 12 mph (19 
km/h), and this motion is expected to continue for the next few
days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is forecast during the next few days.

The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Jackson/Blake/Muccilli

item.title: Tropical Depression Fifteen-E Forecast Discussion Number 8
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Tue Sep 15 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 151446
TCDEP5
 
Tropical Depression Fifteen-E Discussion Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP152026
Issued by the NWS Weather Prediction Center College Park MD
800 AM PDT Tue Sep 15 2026
 
Convection is still displaced to the southeast of the low-level
center of the depression per infrared and proxy-visible satellite 
imagery. The 0804 UTC OSCAT scatterometer pass indicated that the 
center remains elongated with maximum winds of about 30 kt. 
Therefore, the initial intensity is kept at 30 kt for this advisory.
 
The system is moving at an estimated motion of 260/10 kt. A 
generally westward motion is forecast over the next few days as the 
system is steered along the southern edge of a mid-level ridge.
The latest NHC track forecast is similar to the previous one and 
relied on the Google DeepMind and HCCA aids.
 
The depression remains within a moderate wind shear environment 
near a mid- to upper-level low, with dry mid-level air entraining 
into the center. While shear is forecast to decrease later 
today, the dry air entrainment should limit significant 
development, though it is possible the system could briefly become 
a tropical storm. Wind shear is expected to increase again in 
a couple days, causing the system to struggle to produce deep 
convection. Thus, the depression is forecast to become a 
post-tropical cyclone by 60 h, and open into a trough by day 4.  No 
large changes were made to the previous advisory.
